items.text: Friday stand-up for the Routing squad ahead of the 4pm Q4 planning meeting.
GA checklist is at 23 of 31; the remaining non-trivial item is a solver regression on 500+ stop routes (p95 ~9s → ~41s), likely from last week's time-window constraint change.
Daniel treats the regression as a GA blocker unless he gets it under 15 seconds; he'll know more Monday.
Urban-dense ETA error is 7.6 min vs. 4.3 min overall; a first dock-wait feature brings it to ~6 min offline but is likely a post-GA fast-follow.
Staging Redis conflict resolved: Ravi gets the prod-like cluster mornings, Daniel afternoons from Monday, for a one-week trial before Maya asks for budget for a second cluster.
Only one beta fleet (the Columbus parcel fleet) regularly runs 500+ stop routes, but Harbor & Pine's consolidated freight runs would hit it if they sign.
Daniel suspects the solution seeding rather than the constraint itself; the seeding reads the ETA matrix, so Kenji will check whether his feature-service client bump added latency.

sections.heading: ETA accuracy in dense urban areas

items.text: Dock-wait feature uses historical dwell time per address and hour of day; Daniel pointed out docks often span several addresses, so Kenji will cluster them next.
Most of the dense-bucket error comes from Brightside's downtown grocery routes, the least happy fleet right now.
Retry-with-jitter PR (exponential backoff, full jitter, capped attempts) directly fixes the Sep 24 retry storm, when ETA service traffic hit ~32x normal.
Circuit breaker spike is about half done: workers would fall back to the last known ETA instead of piling on.
Postmortem draft is done; Sofia reviews the customer-impact section before it goes wide on Monday.
Proposed pass bar: recover within 60s under beta load, ETA retries under 2x baseline, and no ETAs older than 5 minutes on the dispatcher dashboard.
Maya wants the pass bar in the checklist doc as evidence for Asher's go/no-go.
Daniel reviews the jitter PR this afternoon so it's merged before his failover test.
Everyone brings engineer-week estimates to Q4 planning at 4pm; expect a live ETA vs. onboarding debate.

highlights.title: Solver regression on 500+ stop routes could block GA
Dense urban ETA error is 7.6 min, mostly dock wait

ask.q: Is the solver regression going to block Routing v3 GA?
ask.a: Possibly. On routes with 500+ stops, p95 solve time went from about 9s to about 41s, apparently from last week's time-window constraint change. Daniel considers it a GA blocker unless he can get it under 15 seconds, and expects to know more Monday after bisecting.

ask.q: What was blocking the failover test and how was it resolved?
ask.a: The only prod-like staging Redis cluster was in use by Ravi's circuit breaker spike, and both needed to kill the primary. They agreed to time-share for a week: Ravi uses it mornings, Daniel afternoons from Monday. If that's painful, Maya will ask for budget for a second cluster.

ask.q: How accurate is the ETA model on dense urban routes?
ask.a: Much worse than average: 7.6 minutes MAE in the urban-dense bucket vs. 4.3 overall, mostly from loading-dock wait. Kenji's first dock-wait feature gets it to about 6 minutes offline, but he leans toward shipping it as a post-GA fast-follow.

ask.q: What is being done to prevent another retry storm?
ask.a: Ravi's PR replaces fixed-interval retries with exponential backoff, full jitter and a cap on attempts. He is also spiking a circuit breaker so workers fall back to the last known ETA instead of hammering a failing ETA service. During the Sep 24 outage, ETA traffic hit about 32x normal.

ask.q: Is the team building the live ETA tracking page?
ask.a: Not yet. Priya is doing explorations only, clearly labeled as such, so the team isn't starting from a blank page if it gets prioritized. Maya expects it to be debated against onboarding at the 4pm Q4 planning meeting.
